From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: POC trial planning - success criteria & workload intake

Hi Samantha / Michael,

Great to speak earlier — thanks for the time. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed POC plan, success criteria, and the workload details we need to size the trial. Please review and confirm or flag anything I've missed.

Summary (proposed):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Acme's realtime recommendation endpoint (ML feature service) over a 2-week trial.
- Success criteria (examples):
  - 95th pct latency < 150ms for 1-token outputs (end-to-end, client -> Redwood -> client)
  - Model quality: top-5 ranked suggestions precision >= current baseline (we'll use your eval set)
  - Cost target: <= $0.0008 per generated token (target for comparative analysis)
  - No production-impacting errors; error rate < 0.1%

Evaluation plan / timeline: 
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope, share traffic sample and SOW.
- Week 1: onboarding + dataset ingest + smoke tests.
- Week 2: full load test and metrics collection.
- Deliverable: performance report + recommended configuration + next-step proposal.

Ownership:
- Acme: Samantha (PM) + Michael (SRE) for traffic / procurement coordination.
- Redwood: me (AE) + Marissa Cole (Solutions Engineer) for technical onboarding and trial ops.

Workload intake items required to size the POC (please provide):
1) Typical RPS (steady-state) and expected peak RPS (burst).
2) Average and 95th percentile input prompt length (tokens) and output token length distribution.
3) Expected concurrency (simultaneous open requests) and typical request duration.
4) Payload sizes and any additional pre/post-processing that runs on the client side.
5) SLA expectations and any regional constraints.

Attachments: I attached a draft POC SOW and a small traffic_sample.csv (example format).

Next steps: if you can share the traffic sample + confirm success criteria by EOD Friday, Marissa and I will propose a resource configuration and kickoff date.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: POC_SOW_v1.pdf (stub), traffic_sample.csv (stub)

Thanks Dylan — nice recap. Quick answers below and we'll pull the detailed sample for you by tomorrow.

Answers (high level):
- Steady-state RPS: 30 RPS, expected peak bursts up to 350 RPS (short spikes ~2-3 minutes during promos).
- Token lengths: input prompts avg ~40 tokens (95p ~120 tokens). Output/response avg ~12 tokens (95p ~30 tokens).
- Concurrency: we typically have ~8 concurrent in-prod long-lived requests; during peak we see 60 concurrent.
- No heavy client pre-processing besides JSON enrichment; payloads are small.
- Regional: US east primary; we can route through EU for DR but not required for POC.

We'll attach a 24-hour sample CSV and our eval set for the model-quality comparison. Looping in procurement once we have the SOW.

—Samantha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-19T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC trial planning - Acme (workload answers)

Thanks — reviewed the sample and Samantha's notes. High-level technical plan below.

Short answer: feasible within a 2-week run. Proposed config:
- Model recommendation: medium-sized open LLM (e.g., 7B quantized variant) for the baseline quality test; keep a fallback 13B variant for quality regressions.
- GPU profile: 1x A10G for baseline cluster during POC with autoscaling to 2x for burst windows (short warmup recommended).
- Concurrency / batching: set per-worker concurrency to 8; enable dynamic batching with max batch size tuned to 32 tokens. For 350 RPS bursts we should rely on autoscale + client-side retry/backoff to smooth spikes.
- Expected latency: given 40-token input + 12-token output avg, we estimate p95 ~ 120–200ms depending on model variant. We'll instrument to measure cold-start vs warmed KV cache.
- Cost: I'll run the numbers and share an estimated per-token cost for the proposed config (will include in a short cost appendix).

Instrumentation & trial ops:
- Please ask Acme to provide the eval set and an expected traffic replay script (we can accept the CSV + small script or use a Redwood load runner).
- We'll enable request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdown in the Console for the trial.
- Add health checks and a fallback policy to a smaller variant if error rates increase.

Clarifying question for Acme (please confirm):
1) For the 350 RPS bursts, is that sustained for any period longer than 2–3 minutes? If yes, we should expand baseline capacity.
2) Do you have a strict latency SLO for the trial (SLA) or is this exploratory?

Timeline: we can do onboarding + smoke tests in 2 business days after receiving the sample + eval set. Full load testing on day 7 of the trial window.

I'll draft a short config appendix and cost estimate; can share by EOD tomorrow.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
